A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffCAP research, with matching algorithms and substantial shared experimental content. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioning, VQA, classification, and ablation results, plus adaptive-attack, hallucination, and jailbreaking evaluations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds targeted-attack, perceptual-quality, distribution-shift, and hyperparameter evaluations in the main text and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain cumulative noise injection, consecutive-embedding similarity stopping, threshold calibration, and reverse denoising. The explicit shared-noise assumption concerns the theoretical analysis; alternative schedulers are evaluated as ablations without replacing the proposed default procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST and ImageNet-Sketch evaluations, resolution/long-tail distribution-shift scenarios, targeted-caption attacks on MiniGPT-4, and L2-bounded threats. The retained classification tables are relabeled from ImageNet1K to ImageNet-R without numerical changes; the PDFs do not establish whether that reflects corrected identification or different experiments.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain TeCoA, FARE, JPEG-DL, DiffPure, and CLIPure. Additional evaluations use existing defenses or no-defense controls, sometimes restricting the comparator subset for new settings. AttackVLM supplies additional attacks, rather than a new competing defense.

E3.justification: New protocols include targeted-caption matching with CLIP scores, 16/255 captioning attacks, L2-bounded VQA attacks, PSNR/LPIPS fidelity measurements, batch-one overhead measurements, and fixed-depth DiffPure controls. Appendix D varies calibration sizes and scheduling strategies. Original settings largely persist; D.5's stated default step size of 0.10 conflicts with 0.01 elsewhere, so an actual default change is unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond retained backbone and captioning threshold/step-size ablations, v2 adds quantitative fidelity analysis, under-/over-purification comparisons, and robustness checks under additional threats. Appendix D substantially expands threshold sensitivity testing across calibration sizes, domains, tasks, and encoders, and adds scheduler comparisons. Relocated adaptive-attack results are not new analyses.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix D.1 newly reports three random seeds across calibration sizes and a threshold estimate of 0.958 ± 0.003. v1 lacks this uncertainty reporting. The meaning of the ± quantity is unspecified, and comparable repeated-run uncertainty is not added to the main performance tables.

E6.justification: Matched original tables retain their numerical scores, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 5, 7, and 9–16 and Figure 5. For example, the new MF-ii comparison reports average CLIP scores of 0.730 without defense versus 0.465 with DiffCAP; new fidelity measurements report OF-COCO PSNR of 29.03 for DiffCAP versus 24.27 for DiffPure. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 and Theorem 2 explicitly acquire a shared-Gaussian-noise coupling condition, clarifying their formal scope. Appendix B.3 replaces v1's flawed monotonicity argument with an auxiliary-function argument using H(t) = beta(t)^2 − 2C_beta(1 − alpha(t)). This substantively repairs the reasoning supporting the central decreasing-bound result.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the empirical contribution from consistently outperforming state-of-the-art defenses to outperforming baselines on generation while remaining competitive on classification. The abstract foregrounds recovery and convergence theory, but the central adaptive-purification contribution remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds a conceptual extension from classification theory to prompted VQA and generative VLMs. Appendix D introduces explanations linking semantic richness to threshold selection, threshold/step-size combinations to premature stopping or over-purification, and scheduler variation to recovery behavior. The original image-only limitation and hallucination interpretation are retained, with relocation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access link, detailed BPDA identity-gradient implementation and EOT averaging instructions, calibration and component timing, and further experimental configuration information. It specifies A100 40G hardware and H100 use for hallucination/jailbreaking, replacing v1's blanket A100 description. Previously disclosed diffusion hyperparameters are mainly relocated into the main text.

R1.justification: v2 adds DiffPAD to the purification discussion and references for MNIST, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch, and LPIPS. Positioning against adversarial training and fixed-time purification remains substantially unchanged. Numerous venue updates and consolidated duplicate references represent bibliographic maintenance rather than newly cited research.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and contribution presentation, swaps related work and preliminaries, moves adaptive attacks and the captioning threshold ablation into the main analysis, and moves the principal classification comparison into the appendix. Author statements and a dedicated hyperparameter appendix substantially reorganize the narrative, although much technical prose is retained.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different publication layout and extensively rearranges displays. The old threshold plot becomes main-text Figure 2 with explicit axis labels, qualitative examples are enlarged, and classification and adaptive-attack tables change placement. Ten genuinely new tables and a new VQA sensitivity figure substantially expand the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs a central proof argument and makes its coupling assumption explicit. Quantitative fidelity comparisons and systematic threshold tests address important gaps in v1's support for faithful, reliably adaptive purification; expanded attack evaluations and implementation information further strengthen the paper. These gains go beyond unchanged headline scores. Remaining ImageNet-label inconsistencies and conflicting default step-size statements limit clarity and reproducibility, but do not outweigh the substantial improvements in mathematical reasoning and empirical support.
